title: Two days at home
hook: Could retention improve without a measured performance increase?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish worker-retention outcomes from performance outcomes in the hybrid-work trial.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish worker-retention outcomes from performance outcomes in the hybrid-work trial.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Illustrative quit rates are 6% in office and 4% in hybrid, while performance is 100 in both. What is the relative quit reduction? Toy inputs A=[6, 4, 100, 100]; B=[6, 6, 100, 100].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[33.333333333333336, 2, 0], [0, 0, 0]]. Labels: Quit reduction %, Quit gap pp, Performance gap.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Retention and performance are separate outcomes. The relative quit reduction divides the two-point drop by the original six-percent rate, while the performance gap remains zero in this table. One outcome does not establish a gain in the other.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Office quits %=6, Hybrid quits %=6, Office performance=100, Hybrid performance=100. What is Quit reduction %? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Office quits %=6, Hybrid quits %=6, Office performance=100, Hybrid performance=100. What is Quit reduction %?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Hybrid work two days a week left performance unchanged and cut quits by a third (Bloom, Han & Liang, 2024).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.
